stories.headline: Lens fans banned from Liverpool match for throwing flares vs. Brugge
stories.summary: Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling Tuesday.
stories.body:
NYON, Switzerland -- Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling on Tuesday.

Lens fans lit dozens of flares and threw some toward rival supporters and the field, forcing the team's Champions League game at Club Brugge last week to be stopped briefly. Lens lost 3-0.

The club already were on probation by UEFA for fans lighting flares and fireworks at a previous Champions League game at Slavia Prague in September.

UEFA said its appeals judges imposed a ban on Lens selling tickets to fans for two Champions League away games.

The sanction will be served when Lens play at Leipzig on Nov. 24 and at Liverpool at Anfield on Jan. 27. A third game ban is deferred for a two-year probationary period.

UEFA said Lens were fined €80,000 ($89,000) for charges of "lighting and throwing of pyrotechnics as well as for acts of damage."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Sua Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.

stories.headline: George Russell on disappointing season: 'This year will not define my career'
stories.summary: George Russell has vowed that this season will not define his career as he prepares to watch teammate Kimi Antonelli celebrate his world championship win.
stories.body:
George Russell has vowed that this season will not define his career as he prepares to watch teammate Kimi Antonelli celebrate his world championship win.

Antonelli is likely to become the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history following Sunday's race in Mexico, with four scheduled rounds to spare.

Russell, 28, finished a lowly eighth in Austin last weekend as his 20-year-old colleague stormed to a ninth win of the season, extending his title lead to 123 points with just 125 left to play for.

Russell was at a loss to explain his deficit to Antonelli in Texas but is determined to end the season strongly and head into next year ready to turn the tide.

"I have learnt more about myself this year than I would have liked to in all honesty. Highs and lows in sport are immense and that is because we all care so much what we are doing," Russell said.

"I am 28, Lewis [Hamilton] and Fernando [Alonso] are still competing extremely well in their 40s. Lewis won most of his titles in his 30s, this year will not define my career as a whole.

"It will not break me, it will make me stronger.

"I have generally bounced back very well from difficult moments. Every athlete has seasons where they are not at their best level. Unfortunately this year for me has come at the time I needed it most, but this is nowhere near the end of my journey."

- Sergio Pérez's F1 second act: Red Bull regrets, redemption and a fresh start at Cadillac

- Mexico City Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli to miss media day with viral illness

- Sergio Pérez signs new deal with Cadillac until 2029

Russell's slender title hopes have evaporated over recent races. An engine blow up in Malaysia was compounded by starting from the back of the grid in Singapore, while in the United States he just had no answer to Antonelli.

The British driver finds himself in a scrap to hold on to second place -- although he reiterated his claim from last week that that position would mean nothing to him -- with Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc all within 10 points.

"I think for every driver on the grid there is only one position that matters and it is P1. To be best of the rest is not something you dream of as a kid," Russell said.

"It is more important to finish the season on a positive momentum. Second, third, fourth, fifth -- I will only lose or gain sleep based on performances.

"This sport is kind of P1 or nothing, really."

The Italian has dominated his teammate since the second race of the season, with Russell unable to stop Antonelli's march.

But the Briton stressed he is not worried about comparing himself to his teammate, instead looking at himself as he bids to bite back in 2027.

"The approach I have -- we are not boxers in a ring fighting directly against somebody else," Russell added.

"We are kind of fighting against ourselves. A bit like a golfer. I am not directly looking at my number one competitor saying 'how do I beat this guy?'

"I am looking at myself saying 'what do I need to do'?"

Russell wants to use the final five races, starting on Sunday in Mexico City, to find a consistent level of performance.

"A couple of races ago [Baku in September] we were on pole and won the race. Last week we're finishing eighth," he added.

"I've never had a season like this in my career where the performance has fluctuated so much. I know it it is in there, you can't deliver performances like Baku if you've so-called 'lost it.'

"Just struggling to have a high hit rate, I've never had it personally before in my career. So that is probably the priority for the last few races."

stories.headline: Court revokes pardon for Rays' Wander Franco in sex abuse case
stories.summary: A Dominican Republic appeals court revoked a pardon awarded to the Rays' Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.
stories.body:
SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic -- An appeals court in the Dominican Republic on Thursday granted a request by prosecutors to revoke a judicial pardon previously awarded to Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.

The Dominican Public Prosecutor's Office argued that the lower court's original pardon rested on an erroneous interpretation of legal provisions intended only for exceptional circumstances -- conditions that prosecutors maintained do not apply to Franco's case.

Franco's defense team objected to the motion, but the appellate court ruled in favor of the prosecution, essentially upholding Franco's previous conviction, with a suspended three-year prison sentence. Franco will not be required to serve time in custody provided he maintains a fixed residence and remains under judicial supervision.

Franco was arrested in January 2024 after being accused of having a four-month relationship with a girl who was 14 at the time and transferring thousands of dollars to her mother to consent to the illegal relationship. Franco, now 25, was originally convicted in June 2025.

Six months after that, Tampa Bay placed him on the restricted list, which cut off the pay he had been receiving while on administrative leave. He hasn't played in the majors since.

The court on Thursday imposed the conditional terms considering Franco's age and to support his eventual reintegration into society. If he fails to comply with any of the conditions, he will be required to serve the full three-year prison sentence.

Neither Franco nor his legal counsel offered a statement upon leaving the courthouse.

Franco, who was once the Rays' star shortstop, had signed a $182 million, 11-year contract in November 2021 but saw his career abruptly halted in August 2023 after authorities in the Dominican Republic announced they were investigating him for an alleged relationship with a minor. Franco was 22 at the time.

Following Thursday's hearing, prosecutors reiterated that they had substantiated their charges throughout multiple trials, presenting robust evidence that established the criminal conduct of Franco and of the minor's mother.

The court upheld a 10-year prison sentence for the mother, who was found guilty of commercial sexual exploitation and money laundering.

Additionally, the court ordered the forfeiture of approximately $34,000 found in her possession -- funds provided by Franco in exchange for her consent to his relationship with her daughter.

Franco retains the right to appeal this decision to the Supreme Court of Justice of the Dominican Republic.

Major League Baseball declined to comment.

stories.headline: Vikings and Lions match up NFL's stingiest defense vs. high-scoring offense in NFC North showdown
stories.summary: — The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's only unbeaten team thanks to their stingy defense and stellar special teams.
stories.body:
DETROIT -- — The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's only unbeaten team thanks to their stingy defense and stellar special teams.


If their low-scoring offense doesn't get in gear in the Motor City on Sunday, it might be tough for the NFC North leaders to keep up with the high-octane Detroit Lions.


Minnesota (6-0) is allowing a league-low 12.3 points per game and Detroit (4-2) is averaging 30.7 points, ranking behind only Buffalo, and something has got to give at Ford Field.


“You want to play the best, you want to beat the best,” Lions quarterback Jared Goff said. "You want to have these opportunities to show what you’re made of.


“I think they’re the best in the league right now on paper and certainly present a ton of challenges and it’ll be fun to try to solve those challenges.”


The last time the NFL had a matchup of teams giving up 13 or fewer points and scoring 30-plus points a game in Week 8 or later was in 2019 when Baltimore's high-scoring offense beat New England's stout defense and handed the Patriots their first loss that season.


Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said his confidence in the the team's offense will never waver, knowing the players around him, and believes a breakout performance is coming.


“We’ve just got to end the drive with touchdowns instead of kicking field goals,” Murray said.


That has happened lately.


Minnesota's offense has scored just four touchdowns over the last five games and is averaging just 1 1/2 offensive touchdowns per game, the second-lowest average in the NFL.


The Lions, meanwhile, are rolling with Goff playing as well as any NFL quarterback with one of the league's best running back (Jahmyr Gibbs) and pair of receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams) along with standout tight end Sam LaPorta and a solid offensive line.


The Lions, coming off a win over Green Bay in their first division game of the season, are well aware that the game against Minnesota is potentially pivotal in the NFC North race.


“If you can’t get fired up for this and for the competition of it and in the division, I mean, I don’t know what you can get excited for,” Detroit coach Dan Campbell said. "This is as good as it gets.”


Need to know
Minnesota (6-0) at Detroit (4-2)


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox.


Latest odds: Lions by 3.


Against the spread: Vikings 4-2; Lions 1-4-1.


Last week: Vikings beat Colts 16-10; Lions beat Packers 20-17.


Last meeting: Vikings beat Lions 23-10 on Dec. 25, 2025, in Minneapolis.


Series record: Lions lead 82-45-2.


Matchup to watch
Detroit's balanced offense against Minnesota's blitz-heavy defense. The Lions were 4-0 against the Vikings, averaging 30.5 points a game, in Brian Flores' first two years as their defensive coordinator. In Minnesota's two wins last year, Detroit averaged just 17 points and the Lions had six turnovers in the last meeting. This season, the Vikings have become the third team in two decades to give up 13 or fewer points and 224 or fewer yards in three straight games in a season. Goff has thrown 223 passes without getting picked off, ranking sixth among NFL quarterbacks with the most pass attempts without an interception to start a season. He has 14 touchdown passes without an interception, matching Russell Wilson's run in 2019 for the most touchdown passes without a pick through the first six games of a season. Goff ranks first in the NFL with a 12.5 passer rating, 298 yards passing per game and 14.67 passing first downs a game.


Stats and stuff
— Minnesota, off to its best start since 2009, has a chance to be 7-0 for the first time since 2000.


— The Vikings have won four straight NFC North games and nine of their last 12 in the division.


— Minnesota is an NFL-best plus-7 in turnovers and its seven interceptions rank among the league leaders.


— Detroit has won two straight for the first time this season.


— Gibbs is the only NFL player to run for at least 40 first downs and catch passes for 10-plus first downs through the first six games of a season since the NFL began tracking the data in 1981.


— Detroit’s improving defense allowed an average of 19 points during its two-game winning streak.

stories.headline: Crystal Palace's Ismaïla Sarr set to be sidelined for weeks, Pierre Sage confirms
stories.summary: Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.
stories.body:
Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.

The Senegal international was last season's Conference League top scorer, but has made just five appearances for Palace across all competitions so far.

Palace have lost one of those five games, while they have been beaten in five of the eight matches he has missed, but the under-pressure Sage will have to do without him for at least the next three outings before the November international window.

When asked about when the 28-year-old might be available again, Sage said: "I think after the international break."

The under-pressure Eagles boss secured a big Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday night, and will now look to turn Palace's Premier League fortunes around at Tottenham before hosting Hoffenheim in the Europa League, then welcoming Liverpool to Selhurst Park before the pause.

Asked if he might prefer to be taking on their subsequent league opponents -- Coventry and Hull -- Sage said: "Every point smells good, and if we take points against Liverpool or Tottenham or against the other team, it's the same for us at the end, because we need, and we will play all the game to take points.

"We are not in a position to choose one game better than another. We do, we did, and we will do the same with the cups and the league too. That's why we made some rotations, because we wanted to win on Wednesday, but we wanted to create the conditions of freshness for Saturday too.

"At the moment that strategy is good, but we have to confirm that and go until the goal we fixed at the beginning of the week."

Sage confirmed Jean-Philippe Mateta was rested against Fulham but will be ready to start against Tottenham.

Jorgen Strand Larsen continues to recover from the ankle issue he sustained in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas last week, and will train with the group on Thursday afternoon.

Sage confirmed Quinten Timber could also potentially feature in the Spurs clash, which should also feature captain Dean Henderson who recovered well on his first start back from injury on Wednesday.

Palace sit one place and point clear of the relegation zone heading into Sunday's trip to north London, and there has been some suggestion that this weekend could be a major test of the front office's faith that Sage remains the right man for the job.

- Pierre Sage: 'No noise inside' Crystal Palace despite job pressure

- Animal rights group PETA call for Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot

While Fulham was a "good sign," Sage was wary of using it as a litmus test, given the heavy rotation.

He added: "We change 10 players, and the opponent will be different. That's why it's difficult to take a performance, and without the guarantee it will be the same in another context with other players.

"But the idea, the mindset is here, and now we are sure as a group, as a team, that we are able to do that, but we have to do that in the Premier League.

"For the moment, it's not the case. The good sign was we did this thing in the cup, against a Premier League team."

stories.headline: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope
stories.summary: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced.
stories.body:
Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, on Thursday, the team announced.

Edwards had a debridement procedure performed on his knee, which is a minimally invasive measure used to clean, smooth or remove damaged cartilage, bone spurs or loose joint fragments from the knee joint to relieve pain and improve mobility, according to the Mayo Clinic.

The team's statement said Edwards is expected to make a full recovery but did not denote a time frame for his potential return. Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that Edwards could be sidelined up to two months.

Speaking before Wednesday night's loss to the Warriors, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said he expects Edwards to be "good as new" when he eventually returns to game action.

Edwards, 25, has been bothered by right knee pain since last spring and was limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He was seen grabbing his knee and grimacing at one point during Sunday's home opener against the Toronto Raptors. Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland. His 133 points through four games is a franchise record.

An MRI on Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. His condition this summer was not such that a procedure would have been recommended then, Connelly said Wednesday.

"We're just concerned about his long-term health," Connelly added. "We want to make sure we're putting him in the best position he can be so he can be the best version he's going to be for a long time.

"He's bummed, but Anthony is such a naturally positive and upbeat guy. He's hit all his teammates quickly and said, 'You guys got it,' and we'll roll from there."

Wolves coach Chris Finch said before Wednesday's loss to Golden State that the Edwards news was "a bit of a shock to everybody." Finch, however, feels confident that his team has the depth and experience to navigate an extended stretch without Edwards.

"We'll have to kind of fill that scoring void by committee," Finch said. "Certainly, spreading more shots around the team, everybody likes that. Obviously they've got to go in to make up the point difference."

Information from the Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Stack your fantasy hockey lineups with Sharks, Rangers in November
stories.summary: Plan for November with fantasy hockey lineup advice and player picks for the NHL's unbalanced schedule.
stories.body:
Facing Halloween head-on and a fresh month thereafter, it's once again time to hack the schedule in your fantasy favor, as a way of maximizing every player's opportunity to contribute. Setting the benchmark at six games, as usual -- when another 20 teams, at minimum, are idle -- a handful of teams are worth recognizing when deciding which available players to keep or stream, all else being equal, on so-called slower nights from Nov. 1 to Nov. 30.

The New York Rangers lead the way in competing on seven such occasions when most of the rest of the league is off, while several others do so on six dates. The ability to roll out the following fantasy figures when few others are active, in timely fashion, then bench them when off on busier slates, helps to provide a winning formula in competition where lineups are set every day.

All advance metrics compliments of Evolving Hockey.

More: Rankings | Most added/dropped | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Who to keep or drop | One pick for every team | Sign up

San Jose Sharks

Not only does Ryan Warsovsky's crew compete on more lightly-scheduled dates (six) this coming month than most of the league, but they hop that train immediately post-Halloween. San Jose faces the Calgary Flames, Los Angeles Kings, Minnesota Wild on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday -- when the overwhelming majority of teams are idle -- before visiting Dallas on a busy Saturday. Although not terribly deep in fantasy talent beyond superstar center Macklin Celebrini, the Sharks aren't lacking either. We'll see how long the experiment lasts but, as of this moment, rookie Ivar Stenberg is skating on a top line with Celebrini, in addition to the No. 1 power play. If those two exceptionally gifted, yet different, young skaters can figure out how to forge some dangerous chemistry, Stenberg will start adding to his production numbers quickly. He already has nine points though 13 contests.

In leagues that reward physical play, Kiefer Sherwood remains an appealing option. No one in the NHL is banging their body around more, averaging 5.6 hits per game. While his current collection of two goals and four assists through 13 games serves as mildly underwhelming, Sherwood's individual Corsi metric (44 iCF) suggests he should have more points to show for his shooting efforts. Which means we may be in for a productive bump soon. The physical forward remains available in 66.7% of ESPN leagues.

Peering through the fantasy lens, there's more and more to like from Yaroslav Askarov. After a shakier start, the 24-year-old netminder is holding his own with a .956 SV% and 1.68 GAA in his past three starts. In fact, he's more than holding his own, harboring an 11.4 Goals Save above Expected (GSAx) since initial puck drop, third only to Jesper Wallstedt and Jacob Fowler. Once the Sharks' offense gets humming, and its newly-cobbled defense tightens up a bit, the victories will come easier. If you need a netminder, know that Askarov is available in 84.5% of ESPN leagues.

Vegas Golden Knights

Vegas is another NHL squad that competes on an appealingly staggered schedule beginning next week. Embarking on a road trip to the east coast, the Golden Knights make stops in Boston, Pittsburgh, Detroit, and Buffalo on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Sunday. Fantasy-wise, a rather pleasing slate indeed. While inconsistent, Ivan Barbashev sports tangible fantasy upside. Skating on a No. 1 line with Jack Eichel and Mark Stone and secondary power play, the veteran winger has six points in his past six games. Better yet, according to Evolving Hockey, he should have three goals on the year, not just one. Not a jarring gap by any means, but serves as reminder that Barbashev is a 25-goal scorer in a full season. He's there for the taking in 65.9% of ESPN leagues.

But Vegas's shiniest accessible fantasy gem resides in net. Outside of one singularly deplorable start in St. Louis, Adin Hill has been good to great this season (5-1-0, 2.63 GAA). After Carter Hart suffered an undisclosed injury earlier this week, the Stanley Cup Champ could be much busier for a solid Golden Knights' squad going forward. Hill won't be available in 78.8% of ESPN leagues for long.

New York Rangers

Leading the charge by competing on seven sparser dates through the month of November, the Rangers boast a rather limited list of attractive and available fantasy performers. Still, skating on a line with J.T. Miller, forward Tye Kartye sports growing charm in his first full season with the Rangers. The 25-year-old quietly amassed 14 points in 24 games after joining New York this past campaign, and is on pace for 60 this full round. I also wonder if we're going to see the winger enjoy regular minutes with the extra skater in the not-too-distant future. Right now, New York's power play is middling at best. Ideally, you want to just flag Kartye, and any other Ranger of interest, until the week of Nov. 9, when New York competes on three off nights, against the Edmonton Oilers, Flames and Vancouver Canucks. A rather attractive western Canadian swing as far as fantasy potential production is concerned.

It's also time to keep closer tabs on the return of Joonas Korpisalo. While Dylan Garand lacks NHL experience, the James Reimer experiment isn't going all that well. This reasonably competitive Rangers crew desperately needs a competent, seasoned netminder to shoulder a good portion of the load before Igor Shesterkin returns next year. At last check, Korpisalo was tapped to return in early November. Fantasy managers with issues in net should remain on alert.

Vancouver Canucks

Outside of the crease -- the Canucks lose too often to justify trusting any Vancouver netminder -- there's a small handful of largely available skaters worth investment in deeper fantasy leagues this month, led by Jonathan Lekkerimaki. The rookie is sizzling right now, with four goals and three assists in his past five contests. Rewarding him with heavy minutes on a top-six scoring line, coach Manny Malhotra is clearly pleased with the Canucks' first-round draft pick (2022). Oh, and guess who's now skating on the club's No. 1 power play along with Elias Petterssen, Jake DeBrusk, and Filip Hronek? Right. While Vancouver's game rhythm really starts to shine in the latter half of November, Lekkerimaki merits grabbing now. There's an excellent chance he won't be unaccounted for in two weeks' time.

At the opposing end of the busy-night spectrum, the Kings, New York Islanders, Seattle Kraken, St. Louis Blues, and Washington Capitals play only once when most of the rest of the league is off.

stories.headline: Cavan Sullivan turned 17 last month, but he's already playing like an MLS MVP
stories.summary: Since MLS resumed after the World Cup, Cavan Sullivan has been the league's best player not named Lionel Messi. Does he deserve some MVP recognition?
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union interim manager Ryan Richter remembers it well.

He was mindful of midfielder Cavan Sullivan's mood earlier this season. Sullivan was finding playing time hard to come by for a side that was struggling mightily. Even as Richter was spending most of his time managing the Union's reserve team, he couldn't help but notice the demeanor of a player he first coached as an 8-year-old.

"He was pissed," Richter said of Sullivan in an interview with ESPN. "He wanted a chance to play."

He eventually got it, and he has been taking out that anger on the rest of MLS ever since.

As Sullivan and the Union head into this weekend's game against FC Cincinnati, the 17-year-old is nursing an ankle injury, but his rise has been the story of the MLS season. His 21 goal contributions have already broken the league record for a teenager, eclipsing the 20 recorded by the New England Revolution's Diego Fagundez in 2013. Ditto for goal contributions by a player younger than 17, with Sullivan -- who turned 17 in late September -- breaking the mark of 10 set by Freddy Adu in 2005.

His success has been accompanied by a feistiness, his brilliance often combined with a snarl. Such success has led to chatter that since the resumption of league play following the FIFA World Cup, Sullivan is the league MVP, non-Lionel Messi division.

There is a case to be made for slotting him in just behind the former Argentina captain given the Union's change in fortunes. Prior to the World Cup break, Philadelphia was dead last in MLS, with just seven points from 15 matches. Since the break, the Union have a league-best 39 points thanks to a 12-3-1 record and clinched a playoff spot on Wednesday. That the run has coincided with Sullivan's ascension is by no means a fluke.

When the subject of Sullivan's MVP candidacy is brought up to Richter, one can almost hear the grimace over the phone. Part of Richter's job description these days is to slow the collective roll surrounding his young star, and he's not about to stop now.

"There's time to look back and reflect on stuff like that after the season," Richter said about the MVP talk. "Forget about all the other outside noise of what could be. Let's have a f---ing great session today."

Numbers have also served to cool the MVP talk. According to TruMedia -- which doesn't count secondary assists to the same degree that MLS does -- Sullivan's 15 goal contributions since the World Cup break has him seventh in the league, behind such luminaries as Orlando City SC's Antoine Griezmann (22) and Messi (19). Sullivan's contributions aren't even the most on his own team, with Milan Iloski (18) leading the way. Other players, such as Cincinnati's Evander and Hany Mukhtar of the Supporters' Shield-winning Nashville SC have been utterly consistent over the course of the campaign.

The MVP moniker also gets thrown around rather casually, and with Messi taking up so much of the league's oxygen, it's an easy label to affix to a player like Sullivan who is enjoying a stellar run of form. In some respects, the chatter doesn't do Sullivan any favors. He's still just a teenager -- albeit an extraordinarily talented one -- and the MVP label doesn't tell the whole story of his season.

Sullivan's production seemingly came out of nowhere. His 14 league appearances prior to this season yielded no goal contributions. He had just five in MLS play in 13 league appearances through the end of May, but he logged just 549 minutes. There certainly wasn't any MVP talk during the first half of 2026.

Yet Sullivan's rise wasn't something that just happened. It was the result of some meticulous planning on the part of the Union from the time they signed Sullivan as a 14-year-old, as well as the player's hard work. Every step, from the academy and through the reserve team to the first team, was carefully choreographed. While it's easy to draw a demarcation line pre- and post-World Cup, there were signs of a breakthrough prior to the pause for the tournament, as Sullivan began to get on the field with more consistency. That extended playing time freed up his mind to begin playing closer to his best.

"In the very beginning of the season, if [Sullivan] got 10 minutes here and there, he would try to fit everything into those 10 minutes, and it's hard to play like that," Richter said. "And then towards the end -- I would say the end of the first half of the season -- when he got some extended runs and a couple starts, then he really showed that he could do something at this level."

When Richter took over after manager Bradley Carnell was fired at the end of May, he decided there was no way he was taking Sullivan out of the lineup.

"The first conversation with [Sullivan] was just that he's going to get the chance now, like a real chance, not just put him in and see how he does," Richter said. "It's, 'Cav, I believe that you are a great player at this level and I believe that you can be. Now you get a real opportunity with coaches who believe that fully, and you've got to take it.'"

Sullivan didn't wait for the regular season to try to repay that faith. His mentality has long been one of his best traits, and he was determined to maximize the time that the World Cup break afforded him. He played a match for Union II against the Ivory Coast prior to the World Cup, a period when most of the roster was on vacation. He trained with his brother, Quinn Sullivan, and his father Brendan, a former pro player, to maintain his fitness. He then played in four friendlies against MLS opposition, and impressed every time.

"That was an important period for [Sullivan] because he gained the respect of everybody," Richter said. "And then when the season started, it was no question of 'does he deserve to start?' Of course he deserves to start. He can be a difference maker for us at this level."

Even then, Sullivan's emergence was a bit of a slow burn. He had no goal contributions in his first four matches post-break, but a goal and assist against Necaxa in the Leagues Cup got him going, and there have been no shortage of highlight-reel moments since, for both club and country. These included an audacious back-heel for a goal against San Diego FC that showed jaw-dropping levels of skill and improvisation. Those traits were on display for the United States team against Mexico, when he stole an errant pass from El Tri keeper Raúl Rangel and lobbed him from 35 yards.

Even if Sullivan's campaign has been a few notches below MVP caliber, it has still been a season to savor, and a new face excelling in the league is always compelling. There's also the fact that MLS and the Union won't have Sullivan for much longer; he's slated to join Manchester City in January 2028, shortly after his 18th birthday. With the league calendar changing, all that's left of Sullivan's time in MLS is the 2027 sprint season and the first half of the 2027-28 campaign.

The impulse, then, is to enjoy Sullivan's presence in the league -- and shower him with praise -- for as long as it lasts. And who knows what the next 15 months will bring? This year's MLS Young Player of the Year award seems well within reach, but any future success is predicated on making the most of the present. With the postseason approaching, that is the challenge facing Sullivan and the Union coaching staff.

"This game changes so quick. If you look where the last five months have taken him, where's five months from now?" Richter said about Sullivan. "We have to continue to push every single day, focus on getting better.

"A lot can change in a few months, so let's make that a positive change. Every week that goes by, let's make it a positive. Let's make another step forward. That's my responsibility as his coach, is to continue to help him taking steps forward. I know he has a mentality that he'll continue to push to do that."

If Sullivan does that, then trophies of all sorts should come his way.

stories.headline: Power to burn and a 'trademark' goal: why Ethan Drever has rocketed up draft boards
stories.summary: Growing up an Essendon supporter, Ethan Drever hasn't 'seen anything' like success. But his rise up draft boards could have him in the frame to be his childhood club's first pick, writes Jasper Chellappah.
stories.body:
Ethan Drever had absolutely no choice on his AFL team. As a newborn he was put in an Essendon jumper at the hospital and he's been a Bomber ever since.

It's been a rough 18 years of fandom since, and he's got some thoughts about his dad's decision.

"I'm [born in] 2008, I haven't seen anything!" he tells ESPN with a grin - and a grimace.

"Dad tells me about his success and I'm like, 'You don't have to rub it in like that.'"

The Dons are entering a new era in 2027 under Mark McVeigh and it's being driven through the draft. They snagged Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow, and Dyson Sharp in the first round 12 months ago and now own pick 1 in the upcoming draft.

Drever also has a lot of thoughts about those drafted before him.

"They've got some good young boys in there now. Robey, Sharp, they're gonna be so good.

"I like Farrow. He should be kicking in and doing all that, he needs to be in priority positions. That's what he's gonna be doing in the future.

"Just that halfback, I reckon he's gonna be really good... he's a beautiful left foot kick."

After a dour two-win season the Bombers have first call on Drever, with the 188cm on-baller strongly linked at the top of the board.

He's an electric runner with the intent to tackle, chase, and pressure - something that hasn't been a trait of Essendon's list for a long time.

Asked what he thinks when watching his boyhood club each weekend, Drever's response would prick the ears of all Bombers fans.

"It'd be nice to be out there and sort of help the boys out, that's kinda what I'm thinking!"

The Vic Country MVP and Rebels best and fairest produced a remarkable season. His star has risen from a first-round chance to the very top of the open pool.

He may have the most translatable traits to AFL level of any prospect. Drever is an elite power athlete, recording a 2.92 second 20 metre sprint which comes across in the tape. He bursts out of the contest with driving legs and loves to exit forward of the stoppage to inflict maximum damage.

His ultra consistent season has come about without any injury concerns, something all other top prospects this year haven't been able to say.

"It's been good not to have to sit on the sidelines this year at all and I can just keep playing consistent footy," he says.

"I only missed one [game] which was just after champs, I just had a break."

Drever lays claim to a pretty handy trademark. On six separate occasions this season he's collected the ball -- either out of a stoppage or in open play -- and powered away from opponents into the forward half of the ground.

From there his long running gait and elite top speed helps him separate from chasing defenders and break the paint of 50 to drive home sensational goals.

"I have heard it's called the trademark goal now. I don't know where that's really come from, it's just a natural thing I guess. I just like to run and have a ping from outside 50," Drever tells ESPN.

"Definitely one of my traits is just my power, especially this year. Building up over the pre-season and definitely my two-way running.

"It's the long-term goal to move into the midfield and be a bit of a Jordan Dawson with his two-way running. I love Finn Callaghan, how he plays. Those two are really great role models for me.

"I think Hugh McCluggage as well, I've watched him a lot. I had a meeting with him this year, he's that sort of two-way runner as well and he's been really good for me."

Drever played 13 games for the Rebels this year in amongst commitments with the AFL Academy and Vic Country. He collected the ball 28 times to go with a goal a game, but he's not satisfied with just being an offensive weapon.

The Ballarat local is a tenacious presence in contests with the appetite to chase and tackle, racking up 6.5 per outing to frank his status as the best pure midfielder in the open pool.

At the draft combine he showed off a much-improved engine running a 6:27 minute 2km after going 20 seconds slower in the lead-up. It's a time that will put him towards the front of the pack on day one of pre-season.

Drever knows exactly what's required to be a midfielder at the next level, and he's determined to get there as soon as possible.

"My endurance side was a big goal of mine, obviously at the top level you've just got to be able to run all day.

"Honing in on my fundamentals and trying to get them the best I can as well. That's what the most important thing is because it's the little one percenters that make a difference in the AFL.

Drever is now on the precipice of living out his dream of becoming an AFL player, and it could be for his boyhood club as the top choice in the open pool of the draft.

That won't matter to him, so long as he gets his opportunity to shine on the big stage.

"I don't really care [if I go at pick 1]. It's nice to have my name up in consideration alongside those boys but I'll just be happy to be picked up wherever I go."

stories.headline: Salkilld, Saint Denis to headline UFC Fight Night in Sydney
stories.summary: West Australian Quillan Salkilld will headline a UFC Fight Night lightweight matchup with Benoît Saint Denis in Sydney in February.
stories.body:
West Australian Quillan Salkilld will return to the Octagon in Sydney, after it was confirmed he'll headline the UFC Fight Night with a lightweight bout against Frenchman Benoît Saint Denis on February 7 (AEDT).

Salkilld, 26, is a former Australian rules footballer who turned to MMA after leaving school at 16, and boasts an impressive 13-1 professional record (6-0 in UFC) with five 'performance of the night' bonuses.

The Broome native has won four consecutive fights with a first-round finish, most recently submitting Mateusz Gamrot in their UFC Fight Night clash in Perth in August. He's widely regarded as Australia's next big combat star.

Meanwhile Saint Denis, 30, is one of the lightweight division's most dangerous finishers, and has a 17-4 professional record.

Peter Kloczko, senior vice president of UFC Australia and New Zealand, said the Fight Night -- to take place at Sydney's Afterpay Arena -- would be an "unforgettable event" featuring one of Australia's brightest young stars.

"UFC Fight Night Sydney is set to be another huge moment for Australian fans, and Quillan Salkilld versus Benoît Saint Denis is a main event that delivers everything we look for in this sport," he said in the official release.

"Quillan has been one of the breakout stars of the UFC's lightweight division, while Benoît is one of the most dangerous and exciting finishers in the sport. Bringing this fight to Sydney will make for an unforgettable night."

stories.headline: Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment
stories.summary: After a remarkable year for Bayern Munich and England, Harry Kane becoming the world's best player is the ultimate reward for years of perseverance.
stories.body:
LONDON -- It is nine years since Harry Kane lingered at the back of the London Palladium at the end of a soccer awards show.

The Best FIFA Football Awards in 2017 had just concluded with Cristiano Ronaldo handed the men's top prize in addition to leading a team of the year including Lionel Messi, Neymar, Sergio Ramos and Gianluigi Buffon.

As the audience filed out and a few mere mortals loitered in the hope of a selfie, Kane stood near the exit, casting a longing stare at the winners on stage. He has dreamed all his life of being in their place, considered in the same breath as the game's greats.

On Monday, at the same storied West End venue, about nine miles from his birthplace in Leytonstone, he finally is. Sat next to Lamine Yamal with last year's winner Rodri one place further away, Kane kept company with the elite. And then he joined them.

Last week in Munich, he told reporters he had found the wait to learn the winner "very stressful" for himself and his family. The final few hours on Monday won't have helped. The rain present earlier in the day subsided, but the controversy did not.

Less than three hours before the ceremony was due to start, the official website published a profile of Kane as the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner. Alongside one for Kylian Mbappé and one for Yamal. They were swiftly deleted. The entire ceremony was then delayed by 45 minutes with no official reason given, amid some speculation that the notorious London traffic was responsible.

Kane won on the undercard -- the Gerd Müller Men's Award or the Striker of the Year -- to cheers from the locals in the audience. The raucous reaction from the cheap seats before addressing the crowd was a prelude to what followed. It was palpably welcome but not, by itself, an indication of the big one: Striker of the Year is not decided by vote but simply by goals, and Kane's 73 was the best in the men's game.

Having waited for over a decade to live this moment, a few extra minutes made no difference in the end.

"Wow, wow, wow," he said after taking the stage before thanking Tottenham Hotspur by saying "I wouldn't be where I am without you" in a moment of typical class.

Monday's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose story of relentless professionalism and determined aspiration serves as an exemplar for any young player. British media is often criticized for prematurely building up players to an impossible level, only to then knock them down when that level is inevitably never reached.

Kane has always been a different case. He publicly judged himself against Ronaldo and Messi, two of the best in history, and used their devastating consistency as a target to match.

His numbers since joining Bayern Munich are staggering: 158 goals in 156 matches following a €120 million move from Tottenham in 2023. The Ballon d'Or voting period takes into account August 2025 to the end of the World Cup in July.

He scored 73 goals in 65 matches during that period, won the Bundesliga, the DFB-Pokal, the German Supercup and led England to their best FIFA World Cup finish in 60 years with third place, scoring six times at the tournament.

Back in 2017, "The Best" awards were a competition set up by FIFA as a rival to the Ballon d'Or after five years of partnership with organizers France Football had come to an end. Kane was on the 24-man shortlist for Best Men's Player that year. He finished 24th. Of course, his journey to the summit began much further back.

Coming through the Spurs academy, a young Kane had loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City, where you would find it extremely difficult to locate anyone honest who genuinely believed at the time they were in the presence of a future world-class talent. A nice kid, sure, a hard worker with a future in the game. But one of England's greatest?

Kane broke into Spurs' first team toward the end of the 2013-14 season and a year later was named PFA Young Player of the Year aged 21, making his England debut in the same season. He marked that moment against Lithuania with a goal then, too.

Fame was a novelty at this point. During a Tottenham preseason tour to Sydney, Kane innocently ventured out to a shopping center in his downtime. He was quickly mobbed by so many adoring fans that the club had to scramble a minibus to bring him back to the team hotel.

Kane went on to score 280 goals in 435 appearances for Spurs while breaking Wayne Rooney's all-time goal-scoring record for England. Barring injury, he will break Peter Shilton's appearance record of 125 caps next month, too.

There was, though, perhaps a sense in the buildup that Kane was not quite the global superstar his Ballon d'Or rivals were, most obviously Messi and Mbappé but also, despite his teenage years, Yamal, named Young Talent of the Year for the third consecutive year.

Former Spurs boss Jose Mourinho alluded to this in a conversation with Kane captured by Amazon in their "All or Nothing" series covering the 2019-20 campaign.

"The world looks to English football with an incredible respect but they still think that the movie stars of football belong to other places -- and I think we have to build also your status in that direction," he said.

Kane replied: "That's my aim. When you are at a club like Tottenham, of course we've done well, personally I've done well, but I want to be Ronaldo, Messi ..."

There he goes again. The Ballon d'Or is voted for by one journalist per country of FIFA's top 100 ranked nations, which brings a different dynamic than, say, the FIFA equivalent, which adds votes from national managers and captains.

He had never finished higher than 10th in the Ballon d'Or vote (2024). There are three criteria, listed in order of importance: individual performances, decisive and impressive character; collective performances and titles won; class and fair play.

And despite the Premier League being one of the United Kingdom's most successful global exports, English players have only ever won it five times (Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan twice) and nobody has triumphed since Michael Owen in 2001.

That's more than two decades of unprecedented growth for the Premier League, and yet LaLiga often feels as though it is where the true individual talents reside. Players from Real Madrid and Barcelona have won it 12 times each. Manchester United are the most successful English club in Ballon d'Or history with four.

Kane, of course, left England in pursuit of silverware after a decade of personal achievement but collective frustration at Spurs. In doing so, he has ended up landing both silverware with Bayern and now the highest individual honor a player can attain.

"I am almost speechless," he said. "Being here in London has made it extra special. It made it a good omen for me tonight." Where once he stared at the Palladium stage, now all eyes are on him.

stories.headline: Daly Cherry-Evans won't consider NRL backflip, backs Roosters' Sam Walker move
stories.summary: Without making any promises, Daly Cherry-Evans has ruled out a second season at the Sydney Roosters, while backing the NRL premiers' hardline stance against Sam Walker.
stories.body:
Without making any promises, Daly Cherry-Evans has ruled out a second season at the Sydney Roosters, while backing the NRL premiers' hardline stance against Sam Walker.

Bound for the English Super League, Cherry-Evans insists he has not fielded any phone calls from Roosters coach Trent Robinson or chairman Nick Politis in the wake of the club pulling its multi-million-dollar deal to Walker to remain beyond 2027.

But even if he does, the 37-year-old won't be answering any potential SOS call from the Tricolours.

"No, it's all done. It's all done," Cherry-Evans said on Thursday.

"Look, I'm so proud of my time at the Roosters, but you won't be seeing me back there as a player."

Asked if he promised, the veteran playmaker said "No", but maintained he was content with ending his 16-season NRL career as it started, with a second premiership to go with his 2011 triumph with Manly.

Speaking from experience, having reneged on a lucrative 10-year deal to join Gold Coast to remain at Manly early in his career, Cherry-Evans said he didn't find Walker's situation sad at all.

"Maybe I'm a little too emotionless with these things," he said.

"It's the game, it's the business. I really admire the way that the Roosters have stood their ground on what they believe to be right for the club.

"That's one thing that has really shone through at my time here, is that they will put the club first over any one individual.

"And then from my point of view on Sam, Sam's doing what's best for him and his family and his future, so that's the thing within all of this is - no one's actually done anything wrong.

"Yeah, the emotions get really high and we all want to see people stay and we don't want to see people leave, and I get it, but at the end of the day, no one's doing anything wrong here.

"This is just a contract negotiation."

Cherry-Evans said, as good mates, he'd been in contact this week with Walker, who is in World Cup camp with the Kangaroos in Townsville, and revealed that his grand final-winning halves partner is remaining positive.

"It's hard to rattle Sammy, or maybe he'll never let you know how much he is stressed, or not doing OK," Cherry-Evans said.

"But from what I understand in my conversations with him, he's going well. He's got good family and friends around him.

"I would back Sam to have a really long career in the NRL. We all wanted to see it happen at the Roosters and I'm sure there's a chance it could happen and still happen, but it's a game, it's a business.

"I know we'd love to see our players play for one club, but the likelihood and the reality of that, it just doesn't happen often anymore."

If the Roosters do release Walker from the remaining year of his contract as the Queensland and new Australia representative becomes a free agent on Sunday, youngster Toby Rodwell is being earmarked as the likely No.7 replacement.

"I love Toby Rodwell, and I think he's got a great future ahead," Cherry-Evans said.

"But I'm not playing hypotheticals with you."
